title: Slot stewardship play notes - Nov 10 2026
content:
Context / goal:
We ran a focused workshop this week on 'slot stewardship' — a lightweight concept for treating GPU slots as managed, time-limited resources that can be nudged rather than force-reallocated. The aim: reduce noisy preemptions and improve tail latency during mixed-priority surges without adding more reserved capacity. This doc captures notes, hypotheses, quick experiment results, and action items for follow-up across regions.

Attendees:
- Maya Chen (note-taker)
- Diego Alvarez (ops lead)
- Priya Raman (runtime)
- Samir Patel (sre)
- Jules Martin (solutions eng)
- Several on-call engineers joined for Q/A (#gpu-ops)

What we discussed (high level):
1) Problem framing
   - Preemption spikes during US-East/Europe overlap windows cause 200–400ms tail latency increases for small chat workloads.
   - Bulk backfills from batch workloads amplify eviction storms when regional slots are tight.
   - Current hedging is coarse: whole-node “reserve” allocation or global throttles, which either hurts utilization or increases cold-starts.

2) Slot stewardship pattern (proposal sketch)
   - Treat slots as objects with soft-lease properties: ephemeral, extendable, and observable.
   - Introduce three lightweight controls: grace-window, stewardship-score, and nudges.
     * grace-window: a short time (20–120s) where preemption is deferred if eviction impact is low.
     * stewardship-score: composite metric per slot (priority, recent-evictions, cache-warmth, request-rate).
     * nudges: prefer migrating low-score jobs to opportunistic backfill lanes rather than immediate eviction.
   - Key UX: ops dashboard should show stewardship-score distribution and candidates for nudging.

3) Experiment: "epsilon-tiling" (small-scale runtime test)
   - Goal: validate that a 60s grace-window + simple stewardship scoring reduces preemption cascade.
   - Setup: US-East edge cluster, mixed workload (hosted chat + nightly embedding backfills), ~120 slots.
   - Duration: 6 hours, ramped to 90% utilization for 2 hours mid-test.

Results (quick, noisy):
- Preemption rate: down 28% vs baseline during the ramp window.
- Tail (95th/99th) latency: improved ~120ms at 95th; noisy at 99th (no clear signal yet).
- Cold-starts: up 7% (we moved some backfills to opportunistic lanes; cold-starts were from those lanes).
- Observed side-effect: KV cache fragmentation increased for a subset of pinned model variants; this aligns with expected tradeoff.

Interpretation / hypothesis refinement:
- Grace-window at 60s seems to let short-lived jobs finish and avoids chain-evictions.
- Stewardship-score needs to incorporate a stronger cache-warmth term to avoid moving heavily primed slots.
- Nudges into backfill lanes reduce immediate preemption count but increase cold-start churn; acceptable if the downstream cold-start mitigation (soft-priming) reduces latency penalty.

Immediate action items (owners + ETA):
- Model stewardship-score iteration: add cache-warmth weight and cap change-rate. Owner: Priya. ETA: 2026-11-17.
- Build a lightweight dashboard card for stewardship-score distribution + top 10 nudge candidates. Owner: Jules. ETA: 2026-11-19.
- Run continuity test with soft-priming turned on for opportunistic lanes (pre-warm 1s token/10s sampling). Owner: Diego + runtime. ETA: 2026-11-22.
- Small-scale traffic routing policy (canary): route 5% of production traffic through stewardship-enabled routing. Owner: Samir. ETA: 2026-11-24.

Risks / unknowns:
- Cost regression risk from extra soft-priming; need to quantify $$ impact per 100k requests.
- Complexity: stewardship state needs careful GC to avoid leaking slot metadata across restarts.
- Cross-region interactions: if US-East delays preemptions, other regions may see shifted pressure; need multi-region sim.

Notes from standup snippets (short, informal):
- Diego: "60s grace looked promising; we saw fewer twin-evictions at 11:03am when embedding jobs started."
- Priya: "Kernel hot-paths are fine but cache tracking needs an LRU-ish metric — will prototype."
- Samir: "On-call saw two incidents where nudges delayed an eviction but the slot holder ran past its expected time; we'll add an escape hatch if runtime > grace*3."

Ideas that didn't make the cut (for now):
- Global slow-fall backoff: decrement stewardship-score gradually across the fleet during sustained congestion — deferred, too risky.
- Priority-aware packing: pack like-priority jobs to reduce cross-eviction noise — longer work, track offline.

Follow-ups for next week meeting:
- Present updated stewardship-score formula and simulated multi-region replay (Priya + Samir).
- Dashboard mock and alpha telemetry for nudge outcomes (Jules).
- Cost delta estimate for soft-priming vs. reduced preemptions (Diego + finance liaison).

Reference tickets and threads:
- INFRA-3472: "Slot stewardship prototype" (linked above)
- INFRA-3519: "Epsilon-tiling experiment results"
- Slack thread: #gpu-ops:payload-2026-11-10
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/slot-orch/pull/89

Quick checklist for canary rollout (engineering):
- [ ] telemetry: emit stewardship-score per slot (sampled 1/s)
- [ ] dashboard: top-k nudge candidate table
- [ ] runtime: grace-window flag (default=60s) + escape hatch if job overshoots
- [ ] routing: 5% canary rule + automatic rollback if preemption reduction < 10% or 99p latency increases

Closing notes (tone: working doc):
This is an early sketch — promising signals but noisy. The play here is to keep controls minimal (grace-window, stewardship-score, nudge) and iterate rapidly rather than building a large global arbiter. We agreed that product/solutions should be looped in if we see customer-facing latency regressions during canary.

Questions for reviewers:
- Does 60s feel like a reasonable default across all model sizes? (we may need model-class-specific windows)
- Any objections to emitting stewardship-score telemetry at 1Hz for canary?

-- Maya
